This commit introduces a new pointer type 'kptr' which can be embedded
in a map value to hold a PTR_TO_BTF_ID stored by a BPF program during
its invocation. When storing such a kptr
register must have the same type as in the map value's BTF
a kptr marks the destination register as PTR_TO_BTF_ID with the correct
kernel BTF and BTF ID.
Such kptr are unreferenced
column2: i.e. by the time another invocation of the

column1: BPF program loads this pointer
column2: the object which the pointer points to

column1: may not longer exist. Since PTR_TO_BTF_ID loads (using BPF_LDX) are
patched to PROBE_MEM loads by the verifier
column2: it would safe to allow user

column1: to still access such invalid pointer
BPF helpers and kfuncs should not be permitted. A future patch in this
series will close this gap.
The flexibility offered by allowing programs to dereference such invalid
pointers while being safe at runtime frees the verifier from doing
complex lifetime tracking. As long as the user may ensure that the
object remains valid
column2: it can ensure data read by it from the kernel

column1: object is valid.
The user indicates that a certain pointer must be treated as kptr
capable of accepting stores of PTR_TO_BTF_ID of a certain type
a BTF type tag 'kptr' on the pointed to type of the pointer. Then
information is recorded in the object BTF which will be passed into the
kernel by way of map's BTF information. The name and kind from the map
value BTF is used to look up the in-kernel type
BTF ID is recorded in the map struct in a new kptr_off_tab member. For
now
column2: only storing pointers to structs is permitted.

column1: An example of this specification is shown below:
#define __kptr __attribute__((btf_type_tag(""kptr"")))
struct map_value {
struct task_struct __kptr *task;
Then
column3: user may store PTR_TO_BTF_ID with the type

column1: task_struct into the map
Note that the destination register is marked PTR_TO_BTF_ID_OR_NULL
the verifier cannot know whether the value is NULL or not statically
must treat all potential loads at that map value offset as loading a
possibly NULL pointer.
Only BPF_LDX
column3: and BPF_ST (with insn->imm = 0 to denote NULL)

column1: are allowed instructions that can access such a pointer. On BPF_LDX
destination register is updated to be a PTR_TO_BTF_ID
it is checked whether the source register type is a PTR_TO_BTF_ID with
same BTF type as specified in the map BTF. The access size must always
be BPF_DW.
For the map in map support
column2: the kptr_off_tab for outer map is copied

column1: from the inner map's kptr_off_tab. It was chosen to do a deep copy
instead of introducing a refcount to kptr_off_tab
needs to be done when paramterizing using inner_map_fd in the map in map
case
column2: hence would be unnecessary for all other users.

column1: It is not permitted to use MAP_FREEZE command and mmap for BPF map
having kptrs
column2: similar to the bpf_timer case. A kptr also requires that

column1: BPF program has both read and write access to the map (hence both
BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG and BPF_F_WRONLY_PROG are disallowed).
Note that check_map_access must be called from both
check_helper_mem_access and for the BPF instructions
check must distinguish between ACCESS_DIRECT and ACCESS_HELPER
reject ACCESS_HELPER cases. We rename stack_access_src to bpf_access_src
and reuse it for this purpose.
